name: @olai/fonts
//exports: Two entries, one per READER, which is the split this package exists to make. `.` is what a PAGE reads: the typefaces, the tokens they write, the attribute and storage key a pick lives under — and nothing else, because a browser that draws a picker has no use for a filename. `./build` is what a client BUILD takes: the generated `@font-face` / `:root[data-font="…"]` sheet, and the list of woff2 files that sheet's `src: url(…)` needs under `/fonts/`. One entry rather than two because they are one obligation — a build that takes the sheet and not the files ships a page whose every face 404s. The third product is not a JavaScript export at all: `default.nix` beside them, which converts those files in the Nix store.
//dependencies: None, and that is the shape rather than an accident: this package is a table and two pure functions over it. It has no `effect` because it never fails and never does IO — the one thing that touches the disk is the Nix derivation, which is not JavaScript. A dependency here would be carried into the browser bundle by a client that only wanted to know what a typeface is called.
